name: Programmatic Film
description: A whole narrated film drawn in code on this computer, in one of twelve hand-made looks (chalkboard, whiteboard, blueprint, ink wash, paper pop-up, pixel RPG, newsreel, map explainer, data story, isometric infographic, risograph, Swiss motion): the Palette LLM writes the script and the film page, Kokoro speaks it, Lemo-Opuscar's renderer draws every frame in headless Chrome, procedural sound effects and music are mixed and mastered to -14 LUFS.

execution.service_target: engines/opuscar_engine.py (Lemo-Opuscar renderer, MIT, vendored in tools/opuscar)

source.license: MIT (code only; its CC BY-NC style docs are not used)

best_for: a narrated explainer, lesson or story drawn in a distinct graphic look (chalkboard, whiteboard, blueprint, ink wash, pixel art, newsreel, maps, data stories...)
diagrams, maps and charts that build on the spoken words
films with no footage and no AI video cost
not_good_for: photoreal people, places or live action (use Flow Video or Storyboard & Video)
explaining an uploaded document (use the Document Explainer)
profile_notes: Added 2026-11-17. Renders locally with the vendored Lemo-Opuscar renderer (Node, playwright-core driving the system Chrome, ffmpeg 7+); narration with Kokoro, sound effects with Opuscar's sfx.py, music with MusicGen. The LLM-written page is refused if it uses network, timers, eval or Math.random, and is checked with stills, Opuscar's reading-time check and a vision review before the render.
